arxiv-2102-00055.title: Lower Bounds on Information Requirements for Causal Network Inference Thanks: This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. CCF 19-00636.
arxiv-2102-00055.creator: Xiaohan Kang and Bruce Hajek
arxiv-2102-00055.description: Abstract Recovery of the causal structure of dynamic networks from noisy measurements has long been a problem of intense interest across many areas of science and engineering. Many algorithms have been proposed, but there is no work that compares the performance of the algorithms to converse bounds in a non-asymptotic setting.

arxiv-2201-12647.title: Supercentenarian paradox
arxiv-2201-12647.creator: Vladimir Gurvich, Mariya Naumova
arxiv-2201-12647.description: Abstract Journal: the Notices of AMS And the LORD said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be one hundred and twenty years. Genesis 6:3 What should you wish for the 120th birthday? Have a nice day!

arxiv-2202-02616.title: On a structural similarity index approach for floating-point data
arxiv-2202-02616.creator: Allison H. Baker, Alexander Pinard, and Dorit M. Hammerling
arxiv-2202-02616.description: Abstract Data visualization is typically a critical component of post-processing analysis workflows for floating-point output data from large simulation codes, such as global climate models. For example, images are often created from the raw data as a means for evaluation against a reference dataset or image.

arxiv-2204-11265.title: Large Hall electron mobilities in head-to-head BaTiO 3 -domain walls
arxiv-2204-11265.creator: Henrik Beccard, Benjamin Kirbus, Elke Beyreuther, Michael Rüsing, Petr Bednyakov, Jirka Hlinka, Lukas M. Eng
arxiv-2204-11265.description: Abstract Strongly charged head-to-head (H2H) domain walls (DWs) that are purposely engineered along the [110] crystallographic orientation into ferroelectric BaTiO 3 single crystals have been proposed as novel 2-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs) due to their significant domain wall conductivity (DWC).

arxiv-2208-05840.title: Collinear functions for QCD resummations arXiv: 2208.05840
arxiv-2208-05840.creator: Stefano Catani, and Prasanna K. Dhani
arxiv-2208-05840.description: Abstract The singular behaviour of QCD squared amplitudes in the collinear limit is factorized and controlled by splitting kernels with a process-independent structure. We use these kernels to define collinear functions that can be used in QCD resummation formulae of hard-scattering observables.

arxiv-2210-14979.title: Robust Domain Adaptation for Pre-trained Multilingual Neural Machine Translation Models
arxiv-2210-14979.creator: Mathieu Grosso, Pirashanth Ratnamogan, Alexis Mathey,
arxiv-2210-14979.description: Abstract Recent literature has demonstrated the potential of multilingual Neural Machine Translation (mNMT) models. However, the most efficient models are not well suited to specialized industries. In these cases, internal data is scarce and expensive to find in all language pairs. Therefore, fine-tuning a mNMT model on a specialized domain is hard.

arxiv-2308-11798.title: FORCASTing the spectroscopic dust properties of the WC+O binary WR137 with SOFIA Facilities: SOFIA(FORCAST)
arxiv-2308-11798.creator: Megan J. Peatt, Noel D. Richardson, Peredur M. Williams, Nicole Karnath, Victor I. Shenavrin, Ryan M. Lau, Anthony F. J. Moffat, Gerd Weigelt
arxiv-2308-11798.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Megan J. Peatt, Noel D. Richardson, Peredur M. Williams, Nicole Karnath, Victor I. Shenavrin, Ryan M. Lau, Anthony F. J. Moffat, Gerd Weigelt. WR 137 (HD 192641) is a binary system consisting of a carbon-rich Wolf-Rayet star and an Oe companion star in a 13-year orbit. Near periastron, the winds of the two stars collide and form carbonaceous dust.

arxiv-2309-16578.title: Overcoming the Barrier of Orbital-Free Density Functional Theory for Molecular Systems Using Deep Learning
arxiv-2309-16578.creator: He Zhang, Siyuan Liu, Jiacheng You, Chang Liu, Shuxin Zheng, Ziheng Lu, Tong Wang, Nanning Zheng, Bin Shao, [0.3cm] National Key Laboratory of Human-Machine Hybrid Augmented Intelligence, National Engineering Research Center for Visual Information and Applications, and Institute of Artificial Intell
arxiv-2309-16578.description: Abstract Orbital-free density functional theory (OFDFT) is a quantum chemistry formulation that has a lower cost scaling than the prevailing Kohn-Sham DFT, which is increasingly desired for contemporary molecular research. However, its accuracy is limited by the kinetic energy density functional, which is notoriously hard to approximate for non-periodic molecular systems.

arxiv-2311-13475.title: Machine Translation to Control Formality Features in the Target Language
arxiv-2311-13475.creator: Harshita Tyagi, Prashasta Jung, Hyowon Lee
arxiv-2311-13475.description: Abstract Formality plays a significant role in language communication, especially in low-resource languages such as Hindi, Japanese and Korean. These languages utilise formal and informal expressions to convey messages based on social contexts and relationships. When a language translation technique is used to translate from a source language that does not pertain the formality (e.g.

arxiv-2312-04968.title: NEural Engine for Discovering Luminous Events (NEEDLE): identifying rare transient candidates in real time from host galaxy images 2023
arxiv-2312-04968.creator: Xinyue Sheng, Matt Nicholl, Ken W. Smith, David R. Young, Roy D. Williams, Heloise F. Stevance, Stephen J. Smartt, Shubham Srivastav, Thomas Moore
arxiv-2312-04968.description: Abstract Known for their efficiency in analyzing large data sets, machine learning-based classifiers have been widely used in wide-field sky survey pipelines. The upcoming Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy of Time and Space Survey (LSST) will generate millions of real-time alerts every night, enabling the discovery of large samples of rare events.

arxiv-2407-21436.title: Enriching Thermal Point Clouds of Buildings using Semantic 3D building Models
arxiv-2407-21436.creator: Jingwei Zhu 1, Olaf Wysocki 1, Christoph Holst 1,2, Thomas H. Kolbe 3
arxiv-2407-21436.description: Abstract Thermal point clouds integrate thermal radiation and laser point clouds effectively. However, the semantic information for the interpretation of building thermal point clouds can hardly be precisely inferred. Transferring the semantics encapsulated in 3D building models at Level of Detail (LoD) 3 has a potential to fill this gap.

arxiv-2409-20459.title: Measuring Coherent Radio and Microwave Photons from the Solar Corona
arxiv-2409-20459.creator: Liang Chen, Zizang Qiu, Thomas W. Kephart, Arjun Berera
arxiv-2409-20459.description: Abstract The rates of production of radio/microwave N-identical photons states | N ⟩ \ket{N} from stimulated emission in the solar atmosphere are estimated. Effects of various decohering factors are shown to be small. Ground based measurements of these quantum states via the inverse HOM effect are proposed.

arxiv-2506-04954.title: The Data Dilemma: Authors’ Intentions and Recognition of Research Data in Educational Technology Research
arxiv-2506-04954.creator: Sandra Schulz 1 \orcidlink 0000-0002-2254-6579, Natalie Kiesler 2 \orcidlink 0000-0002-6843-2729 1 University of Hamburg, Germany 2 Nuremberg Tech, Germany
arxiv-2506-04954.description: Abstract Educational Technology (EdTec) research is conducted by multiple disciplines, some of which annually meet at the DELFI conference. Due to the heterogeneity of involved researchers and communities, it is our goal to identify categories of research data overseen in the context of EdTec research.

arxiv-2506-15031.title: Studying the diffusion mechanism of cosmic-ray particles
arxiv-2506-15031.creator: Ya-Wen Xiao, Jian-Fu Zhang ,, Siyao Xu
arxiv-2506-15031.description: Abstract Context. More and more observations have indicated the existence of slow diffusion phenomena in astrophysical environments, such as around the supernova remnants and pulsar γ \gamma -ray halos, where the diffusion coefficient of cosmic rays (CRs) near the source region is significantly smaller than that far away from the source region.

arxiv-2512-13650.title: Why do we Need Observers? Spontaneous Breaking of Time-Reversal in de Sitter Space.
arxiv-2512-13650.creator: Leonard Susskind
arxiv-2512-13650.description: Abstract In this paper I explain the relation between the need for observers in de Sitter space and the spontaneous breakdown of time-reversal symmetry. 1 The Need for Observers In this note I will address the need for observers in de Sitter space [ 1 ] , especially in the holography of a static patch.

arxiv-2601-04055.title: Modular Prompt Optimization: Optimizing Structured Prompts with Section-Local Textual Gradients
arxiv-2601-04055.creator: Prith Sharma, Austin Z. Henley
arxiv-2601-04055.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as general-purpose problem solvers, where behavior is controlled primarily through prompting rather than task-specific training [ 21 , 4 ] . In practice, prompt quality often becomes the main limiting factor. Small changes in wording, order, or formatting can lead to large differences in model performance, reliability, and even safety.

plos-pbio-0020351.description: PLOS ONE research article. The chytrid fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis has been implicated in the decline and extinction of numerous frog species worldwide. In Queensland, Australia, it has been proposed as the cause of the decline or apparent extinction of at least 14 high-elevation rainforest frog

pmc-11323688.title: The effect of electrical stimulation in critical patients: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-11323688.creator: Lili Li, Fei Li, Xinyin Zhang, Yuying Song, Shuyan Li, Huiping Yao
pmc-11323688.description: ObjectivesWhile electrical stimulation has been demonstrated to improve medical research council (MRC) scores in critically ill patients, its effectiveness remains a subject of debate. This meta-analysis aimed to discuss recent insights into the effectiveness of electrical stimulation in improving muscle strength and its effects on different clinical outcomes in critically ill adults.

pmc-11672199.title: Editorial: Plant metabolites in drug discovery: the prism perspective between plant phylogeny, chemical composition, and medicinal efficacy, volume III
pmc-11672199.creator: Da-Cheng Hao, Yao-Xuan Wang, Richard W. Spjut, Chun-Nian He
pmc-11672199.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). d similar bioactivities. This is the simple core idea of “Pharmacophylogeny,” and the proposed term “Pharmacophylomics” aims to disentangle the intricate relationships and connectivity between medicinal plant phylogeny, phytochemical constituents and bioactivities/therapeutic utilities based on emerging omics data (Figure 1) (Hao and Xiao, 2023); the genomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic data are very useful to promote pharmaceutical resource discovery and plant-based drug R&D.

pmc-11675077.title: Acute Myeloid Leukaemia and Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia Classification and Metabolic Characteristics for Informing and Advancing Treatment
pmc-11675077.creator: Carrie Wemyss, Emily Jones, Régis Stentz, Simon R. Carding
pmc-11675077.description: Simple SummaryThis review focuses on the classification, risk stratification, and metabolic characteristics of acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) and acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) and their importance in the advancement of treatment. It discusses current management strategies, including standard chemotherapy regimens and targeted therapies, while highlighting the challenges of drug toxicity and resistance.

pmc-11739045.title: Paediatric Catatonia as a First Presentation of Autism: A Case Report
pmc-11739045.creator: Vinay Mandagere, Helen Stephens, Kitty Kwan, Jatinder Singh, Paramala Santosh
pmc-11739045.description: AimsCatatonia is a rare neuropsychiatric syndrome in children. It is characterised by mutism, stupor, posturing, negativism, and rigidity. Historically, catatonia was associated only with psychosis, however catatonic symptoms are being recognised as more prevalent in people with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).

pmc-12633951.title: Multi-physics modeling for ion homeostasis in multi-compartment plant cells using an energy function
pmc-12633951.creator: Guillaume Mestdagh, Alexis De Angeli, Christophe Godin
pmc-12633951.description: Plant cells control their volume by regulating the osmotic potential of their cytoplasm and vacuole. Water is attracted into the cell as the result of a cascade of solute exchanges between the cell subcompartments and the cell surroundings, which are governed by chemical, electrostatic and mechanical forces.

pmc-13056290.title: PTEN Loss Promotes PI3Kβ Phosphorylation and EPHA2/SRC/p-PI3KβY962 Complex Assembly to Drive Tumorigenesis
pmc-13056290.creator: Shuang Tang, Qian Zhou, Johann S. Bergholz, Tao Jiang, Weihua Wang, Renlei Ji, Wendi Huang, Jiachen Wu, Yutong Li, Xiaochun Wan, Xiadi He, Qianchen Jing, Menghong Sun, Jared L. Johnson, Tomer M. Yaron-Barir, Da-Qiang Li, Bo Dai, Zefeng Wang, Xiaoling Li, Lewis C. Cantley, Thomas M. Roberts, Jean J.
pmc-13056290.description: PTEN loss promotes PI3Kβ phosphorylation and EPHA2–SRC–PI3Kβ complex signaling to drive tumorigenesis, revealing PI3Kβ phosphorylation as a druggable vulnerability and biomarker for targeted therapy in PTEN-deficient cancers. Introduction The PI3K pathway is hyperactivated across human cancers through genetic PI3K mutations or loss of the PTEN tumor-suppressor (1–3), making the PTEN–PI3K axis a critical therapeutic target.

pmc-13369701.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based clinical decision support tool for stratifying intravenous medication risk in hospitalized patients with heart failure
pmc-13369701.creator: Yang Yang, ZeJie Xu, Yu Peilin, Haidong Li, Hongmei Wang, Xuefeng Shan
pmc-13369701.description: IntroductionHospitalized patients with heart failure (HF) frequently receive multiple high-risk intravenous (IV) medications, placing them at a substantial risk of clinically significant drug-related problems (DRPs). Timely severity-based stratification of IV medication-related risks remains challenging, particularly in the context of complex regimens and organ dysfunction.

pmc-13473093.title: Design of a multi-epitope Staphylococcus aureus vaccine integrating a protein A variant, α-hemolysin, and fibronectin-binding protein A through reverse vaccinology
pmc-13473093.creator: Hannia Michelle Prieto-Nevárez, Alejandro Tarango-García, Arturo Gutiérrez-Guerrero, Aristóteles Álvarez-Cardona, Saul O. Lugo-Reyes
pmc-13473093.description: Staphylococcus aureus has become a major public health concern because of its increasing antibiotic resistance. Given limited clinical success of previous S. aureus vaccine candidates, this study aimed to design and computationally evaluate a novel multi-epitope construct integrating sequences derived from fibronectin-binding protein A, α-hemolysin, and a detoxified protein A variant.
